title: Openness of the flat locus (finite presentation)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module, i.e. $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(S^{\oplus s}\to S^{\oplus t})$ for some $s,t\ge0$ and some $S$-linear map. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ let $M_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $M$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], an $R$-module via $\varphi$. Then the set $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S: M_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is a flat }R\text{-module}\}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$ with its Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (the topology whose closed sets are the sets $V(J)=\{\mathfrak q:\mathfrak q\supseteq J\}$, $J\subseteq S$ an ideal).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ at which $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$, and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] (Stacks 00R1) to obtain a directed system $(R_\lambda\to S_\lambda,M_\lambda)$ with the colimit and base-change isomorphisms in that node. Let $\mathfrak q_\lambda\subset S_\lambda$ and $\mathfrak p_\lambda\subset R_\lambda$ be the inverse images of $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p$. Every $R_\lambda$ is Noetherian: $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $R_\lambda$ is finite type over it, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applies. Similarly $S_\lambda$ is Noetherian, and its localization at $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is a finitely generated module over itself; $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ is finitely generated over $(S_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ because images of the finite generators of $M_\lambda$ generate its fractions. The transition maps on the prime localizations are local homomorphisms, since the preimage of each later prime is the earlier one [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 00RC (theorem-openness-flatness), proof, lines 33427-33441; Lemma Tag 00R1 (lemma-limit-module-finite-presentation)

proof.text: The systems $A_\lambda=(R_\lambda)_{\mathfrak p_\lambda}$, $B_\lambda=(S_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ and $N_\lambda=(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ meet the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat]. Their ring colimits are $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime]. Their module colimit is $M_{\mathfrak q}$: a fraction $m/s$ comes from a common stage containing a representative of $m$ and $s$ by the colimit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation]; if $m/s=0$, a multiplier $t\notin\mathfrak q$ kills $m$, and the equality $tm=0$ holds at a later stage by the elementwise description in [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] applied to the module system of 00R1, so the fraction dies there. Noetherianity and finite generation were checked in step 1, and the transition maps are local. For hypothesis (a), the ring $B_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu$ is the localization of $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\cong S_\mu$ (the isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation]) first at the images of $S_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q_\lambda$ and $R_\mu\setminus\mathfrak p_\mu$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base]; localizing further at $S_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q_\mu$ gives $B_\mu$, since each earlier denominator avoids $\mathfrak q_\mu$. For (b), localize the isomorphism $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\cong M_\mu$ from [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] at $S_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q_\mu$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] to identify the left side with $N_\lambda\otimes_{B_\lambda}B_\mu$. Finally $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], since elements of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ act invertibly on $M_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] yields an index $\lambda$ for which $N_\lambda$ is flat over $A_\lambda$, hence flat over $R_\lambda$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-flat-locus-neighborhood] to $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, the finite $S_\lambda$-module $M_\lambda$ and $\mathfrak q_\lambda$: $R_\lambda$ is Noetherian, $S_\lambda$ is finite type over it (step 1), and $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ (step 2). This gives $g_\lambda\in S_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q_\lambda$ such that $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak r_\lambda}$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ for every prime $\mathfrak r_\lambda$ avoiding $g_\lambda$. Let $g$ be the image of $g_\lambda$ in $S$. Since $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 00RC (theorem-openness-flatness), proof, lines 33446-33457 and the Noetherian argument at lines 33459-33507

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak r\subset S$ avoid $g$ and put $\mathfrak r_\lambda$ for its inverse image in $S_\lambda$; then $g_\lambda\notin\mathfrak r_\lambda$, so $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak r_\lambda}$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ by step 3. Its base change $P=(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak r_\lambda}\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. By the base-change isomorphisms $S=S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ and $M=M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S$ in [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] identifies $M_{\mathfrak r}$ with a further localization of $P$ at the image of $S\setminus\mathfrak r$; the elements of $S_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak r_\lambda$ already act invertibly on $P$. This further localization remains flat over $R$: for every injection $U\hookrightarrow V$ of $R$-modules, $U\otimes_RP\hookrightarrow V\otimes_RP$ is injective by flatness of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; localizing this injection at the indicated multiplicative set preserves injectivity [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] identifies the resulting map with $U\otimes_RM_{\mathfrak r}\to V\otimes_RM_{\mathfrak r}$. Hence $M_{\mathfrak r}$ is flat over $R$. We have proved $D(g)\subseteq\{\mathfrak r:M_{\mathfrak r}\text{ flat over }R\}$, and $D(g)$ is open by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every prime in the flat locus can play the role of $\mathfrak q$, so that locus is the union of these basic open neighborhoods and is open.
